content: This medication is a prodrug, meaning it is converted in the body to its active form, desglymidodrine, which is responsible for its therapeutic effects. Midodrine should only be prescribed to carefully selected patients whose quality of life is significantly impaired despite standard treatments for orthostatic hypotension. To minimize this risk, patients are advised to take the medication no later than 6 PM and at least 3-4 hours before bedtime. This medication is contraindicated in patients with severe organic heart disease, supine hypertension, acute renal disease, urinary retention, pheochromocytoma, or thyrotoxicosis. Additionally, caution is advised in patients with diabetes, vision problems, or renal or hepatic impairment. Midodrine may also slow the heart rate due to vagal reflexes, so it should be used cautiously with other medications that decrease heart rate, such as digoxin or beta-blockers. If bradycardia (slow heart rate) occurs, the medication should be discontinued.g., phenylephrine, pseudoephedrine, ephedrine, dihydroergotamine, thyroid hormones, or droxidopa). Midodrine should not be used with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or linezolid due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. Patients taking midodrine should also avoid medications that may cause vasoconstriction. Common side effects of midodrine include paresthesia (tingling sensations), piloerection (goosebumps), pruritus (itching), supine hypertension, urinary retention or urgency, chills, abdominal pain, rash, anxiety, dizziness, dry skin, flushing, headache, insomnia, nausea, somnolence, and weakness. Midodrine undergoes enzymatic hydrolysis in the systemic circulation, converting it to desglymidodrine, which is 15 times more potent than the parent drug. The half-life of desglymidodrine is approximately 3-4 hours, while midodrine itself has a half-life of about 25 minutes. The drug is primarily excreted in the urine (80% as desglymidodrine) and to a lesser extent in feces (1-2%). It is dialyzable in patients undergoing hemodialysis. Midodrine is classified as pregnancy category C, meaning its safety during pregnancy has not been established, and it is unknown whether it is excreted in breast milk. Therefore, its use during pregnancy or lactation should be avoided unless absolutely necessary.
